Likewise, when an added alif and lām meet it, if you wish you drop the yāʾ because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, and if you wish you give it fatḥa so that two vowelless letters do not come together; but the best of that is fatḥa, as in the words of Allah the Blessed and Exalted ﴿جَآءَنِيَ ٱلْبَيِّنَاتُ مِن رَّبِّي﴾ and ﴿نِعْمَتِيَ ٱلَّتِي﴾ and the like; and that is how we read. If a connecting alif without lām meets it, you also have the choice in it, except that the best in this case is dropping [the yāʾ], and that is how we read: ﴿إِنِّي ٱصْطَفَيْتُكَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ﴾ and ﴿ هَارُونَ أَخِي ٱشْدُدْ بِهِ أَزْرِي﴾.
When any of this is in the vocative, the yāʾ is dropped from it, as in ﴿يٰعِبَادِ فَٱتَّقُونِ﴾, ﴿رَبِّ قَدْ آتَيْتَنِي مِنَ ٱلْمُلْكِ﴾ and ﴿رَّبِّ إِمَّا تُرِيَنِّي مَا يُوعَدُونَ﴾.
Some Arabs drop these yāʾs in the vocative and elsewhere, in everything. That is ugly and rare, except what is at the ends of verses (ruʾūs al-āy), where it is dropped in the pause, just as the Arabs drop [letters] from rhymes in their poetry, as in his saying [in the ṭawīl metre; this is the forty-fourth evidentiary verse]:
[أَبا مُنْذِرٍ أفنيتَ فاستبقِ بعضَنا] * حنانيكَ بعضُ الشرِّ أَهونُ من بَعْضِ
(Abū Mundhir, you have destroyed [us], so spare some of us; have mercy — some evil is lighter than other.)
and his saying [in the wāfir metre; this is the forty-fifth evidentiary verse]:
[ألا هُبِّي بِصَحْنِكِ فاصبَحينا] * وَلا تُبْقِي خُمورَ الأنْدَرينَ
(Ho, rise with your bowl and give us the morning draught, and do not spare the wines of al-Andarīn.)
[that is,] when they pause; when they connect, they say "من بعضِي" and "الأنْدرينا". [Translator's note: the source prints "من بعض" here; the sense requires the restored long vowel.] That is frequent at the ends of verses, as in His words ﴿بَل لَّمَّا يَذُوقُواْ عَذَابِ﴾ [and] ﴿وَإِيَّايَ فَٱتَّقُونِ﴾: when they connect, they keep the yāʾ. Some people dropped the yāʾ both in pause and in connection, following that rare dialect; this is the reading of the generality [of readers], and that is how we read, because the written text follows it.
Some people paused with the yāʾ and connected with the yāʾ; that goes against the written text, because the written text has no yāʾ in it, though it is the good dialect form. We heard an eloquent Arab reciting [in the ṭawīl metre; this is the forty-sixth evidentiary verse]:
فما وَجَدَ النَّهْدِيُ وَجْداً وَجَدْتُهُ * ولا وَجَدَ العُذْرِيُّ قبلِ جَمِيلُ
(Neither the Nahdī felt a passion like the one I felt, nor the ʿUdhrī, Jamīl, before me.)
He means "قبلِي" (before me), and dropped the yāʾ. Some treated "قَبْل" as one treats what has no yāʾ, saying "قبلُ جميل" while meaning "قبلي", just as some Arabs said "يا ربُّ اغفِر لي" (O Lord, forgive me) with the nominative ending, meaning "يا ربّي" (O my Lord).
As for His words ﴿وَتَظُنُّونَ بِٱللَّهِ ٱلظُّنُونَاْ﴾ and ﴿أَضَلُّونَا ٱلسَّبِيلاْ﴾, the alif is kept in them because they are verse-endings; for some Arabs, namely the people of the Hijaz, make the ends of rhymes, when they pause on them, the same as when they connect them. All the Arabs, when they chant rhymes, keep yāʾ, wāw and alif at their ends.
As for His words ﴿يٰأَبَتِ إِنِّيۤ أَخَافُ﴾, He made this noun feminine with the hāʾ [i.e. tāʾ marbūṭa], as in your saying "رجُلٌ رَبْعَةٌ" (a man of middle height) and "غُلامٌ يَفَعَةٌ" (a youth near puberty); or He may have inserted it as compensation for what was removed from the noun. Some read it with fatḥa, as if they meant "يا أبتا" and dropped the alif just as they drop the yāʾ, as the poet said [in the wāfir metre; this is the forty-first evidentiary verse]:
[ولست بمدرك ما فات مني] * "لهفَ" ولا بـ"ليتَ" ولا لَوَآني"
(I shall not recover what has escaped me by "alas", nor by "would that", nor by "if only I…")
He means "لَهْفاه" (alas!). What shows you that this noun was made feminine with the hāʾ is the poet's saying [in the ṭawīl metre; this is the forty-seventh evidentiary verse]:
تقولُ ابنتي لما رأتنِيَ شاحِباً * كأنَّكَ فينا يا أَبات غريبُ
(My daughter says, when she sees me pale: "Father, it is as though you were a stranger among us.")
He restored the alif and added the hāʾ to it, just as it was made feminine in his saying "يا أمتاه" (O mother!); so these are three letters. Some Arabs say "يا أمَّ لا تفعلي" (Mother, do not do it), shortening it (tarkhīm), as he said "يا صاحِ" (O companion). Some say "يا أميّ" and "يا أبي", in the dialect of those who say "يا غلامِي" (O my servant). And some say "يا أبِ" and "يا أمِّ", and this is the good one by analogy.

akhfash:83-83.t:
His saying ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَ بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ لاَ تَعْبُدُونَ إِلاَّ ٱللَّهَ﴾.
And His saying ﴿وَبِٱلْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَاناً﴾: He made it a command, as though He were saying "and goodness to parents", i.e. "do good, a doing of good".
And He said ﴿وَقُولُواْ لِلنَّاسِ حُسْناً﴾: it is on one of two aspects. Either "الحُسْنِ" is meant as "الحَسَنَ" (what is good), just as you say "البُخْل" and "البَخلَ" (miserliness); or He made "الحُسْنَ" (goodness) be "الحَسَنَ" by way of comparison, just as you say "إنَّما أَنْتَ أَكلٌ وشُرْبٌ" ("you are nothing but eating and drinking"). The poet said [in the wāfir metre; it is the hundred and eighth shāhid (evidentiary verse)]:
وَخَيْلٍ قدْ دَلَفْتٌ لَها بِخَيْلٍ * تَحِيَّةُ بَيْنِهِمْ ضَرْبٌ وَجِيعٌ
(Many a troop of horse I advanced against with horse, the greeting between them a painful blow.)
"دَلَفْتُ" means "I headed for"; and he made the greeting a blow. This word is not frequent in speech, but it has come in the Quran. Some of them read it ﴿حَسَنا﴾, meaning "say to them something good". And some of them said ﴿قولوا للناسِ حُسْنى﴾, making it feminine and not giving it tanwīn; and this hardly occurs, for "الحُسْنى" is only spoken with the alif and lām, just as its masculine is only spoken with the alif and lām. [So] if you said "جاءَني أَحْسَنُ وأَطْوَلُ" ("a better and a taller came to me"), it would not be good until you say "جاءَني الأَحْسَنُ والأَطْوَلُ" ("the better and the taller came to me"); and so with this, one says "جاءَتْنِي الحُسْنى والطُولى". Except that they have made some things of this kind nouns, such as "دُنْيا" (world) and "أُوْلَى". The rajaz poet said [it is the hundred and ninth shāhid]:
* في سَعْيِ دُنْيا طالَ ما قَدْ مَدَّتِ *
(In striving for a world that has long stretched [its span].)
And they say "هي خَيْرَةُ النِساءِ" ("she is the best of women") ["هنّ خَيْراتُ النِّساء"]; they hardly use it in the singular, though its singular use is permissible. And in the Book of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فِيهِنَّ خَيْرَاتٌ حِسَانٌ﴾. That is because He did not intend [the pattern] "أَفْعَلَ" (elative); He only intended the feminine of "خير", because when one describes and says "فلانٌ خَيْرٌ" ("so-and-so is good"), it resembles the adjectives, so the hāʾ [tāʾ marbūṭa] was added for the feminine.
As for His saying ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَ بَنِيۤ إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾, then He said ﴿وَقُولُواْ لِلنَّاسِ حُسْناً﴾, then He said ﴿ثُمَّ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ مِّن بَعْدِ ذٰلِكَ﴾: it is because He addressed them after having spoken about them [in the third person]; and this is frequent in speech and poetry. The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the hundred and tenth shāhid]:
أسيئي بِنا أوّ أَحْسِنِي لا مَلُومَةٌ * لَدَيْنا وَلا مَقْليةٌ إِنْ تَقَلَّبِ
(Treat us badly or treat us well — [you are] not blamed by us, nor hated, if [she] hates.)
They only mean "تَقَلَّيْتِ" ("you hated"). And the other said [in the kāmil metre; it is the hundred and eleventh shāhid]:
شَطَّتْ مُزارَ العاشِقينَ فأصبحَتْ * عَسِراً عَلَيَّ طِلابُكِ ابْنَةٌ مَخْرَمِ
(She has gone far from the visiting-place of lovers, and seeking you, daughter of Makhram, has become hard for me.)
He only meant "and the daughter of Makhram became hard for me, the seeking of her". It is permissible to make the speech as though he addressed her, because when he said "she has gone far from the visiting-place of lovers", it is as though he said "you have gone far from the visiting-place of lovers", since it is she he means by this speech. Like it, of what departs from its beginning, is his saying [in the rajaz metre; it is the hundred and twelfth shāhid]:
* إنَّ تَميماً خُلِقَتْ مَلْمُوما *
(Tamīm was created compact.)
He meant the tribe by his saying "خُلِقَتْ" [feminine], then said "مَلْمُوما" [masculine] with reference to the clan or the man; and for that reason he said:
* مثلَ الصَّفا لا تَشْتَكِي الكُلُوما *
(Like the smooth rock, not complaining of wounds.)
Then he said:
* قَوماً تَرَى واحدَهُم صِهْمِيما *
(A people whose every one you see to be a fierce, unyielding man.)
So he brought the plural, because he meant the tribe or the clan. Then he said:
* لا راحِمَ الناسِ ولا مُرْحُوما *
(Neither showing mercy to people nor shown mercy.)
And the poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the hundred and thirteenth shāhid]:
أقولُ لَهُ والرمحُ يأطِرُمَتْنَهُ * تأَمَّل خُفافاً إِنَّنِي أَنَاذلِكا
(I say to him, while the spear bends his back: "Look well at Khufāf — I am that one.")
And [also recited] "تَبَيَّنْ خْفافاً"; he means "I am he". And in the Book of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا كُنتُمْ فِي ٱلْفُلْكِ وَجَرَيْنَ بِهِم﴾: He spoke in the wording of the absent [third person] while it had been in address, because that indicates the meaning. And al-Aswad said [in the basīṭ metre; it is the hundred and fourteenth shāhid]:
وَجَفْنَةٍ كإِزاءِ الحَوْضُ مُتْرَعَةٍ * ترى جَوانِبَها بِالشَّحْمِ مَفْتُونا
(Many a huge bowl, like the spout of a trough, filled to the brim — you see its sides plastered with fat.)
This would be on [the basis] that he took it according to the meaning, i.e. you see every side of it; or he made the attribute of the plural singular, as in what has come in speech. And his saying "مأطِرُ مَتْنَه" [Translator's note: the verse has «يأطِرُ»] means it bends his back. Likewise ﴿ٱلْحَمْدُ للَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾, then He said ﴿إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ﴾, because the one spoken about is the one addressed. Ruʾba said [in the rajaz metre; it is the hundred and fifteenth shāhid]:
الحَمْدُ لِلّهِ الاَعَزِّ الأَجْلَلِ * أَنْتَ مَلِيكُ الناسِ ربّاً فَاقْبَلِ
(Praise be to Allah, the Mightiest, the Most Majestic; You are the King of people, as Lord, so accept.)
And Zuhayr said [in the wāfir metre; it is the hundred and sixteenth shāhid]:
فإنّي لَوْ أُلاقِيكَ أجْتَهَدْنَا * وكانَ لِكُلِّ مُنْكَرَةٍ كِفاء
فأُبْرِىءَ مُوضَحاتِ الرأسِ مِنْهُ * وَقَدْ يَشْفِى من الجَرَبِ الهِناءُ
(If I were to meet you, we would strive [against each other], and every outrage would have its match; and I would heal the head-wounds [I gave] from him [Translator's note: the shift from "you" to "him" is the point of the citation] — and tar sometimes cures mange.)
And Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said ﴿ذُوقُواْ فِتْنَتَكُمْ هَـٰذَا ٱلَّذِي كُنتُمْ بِهِ تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ﴾: He used the masculine after the feminine, as though He meant "this is the matter which you used to seek to hasten". Like it is ﴿فَلَماَّ رَأَى ٱلشَّمْسَ بَازِغَةً قَالَ هَـٰذَا رَبِّي هَـٰذَآ أَكْبَرُ فَلَمَّآ أَفَلَتْ﴾: this would be on [the basis of] "what I see is my lord", i.e. this thing is my lord. And this resembles what the commentators said on ﴿أُحِلَّ لَكُمْ لَيْلَةَ ٱلصِّيَامِ ٱلرَّفَثُ إِلَىٰ نِسَآئِكُمْ﴾: he said: "إلى" only came in because the meaning of "الرَفَث" (sexual approach) and "الأفْضاء" (going in to) is one, so it is as though He said "going in to your wives"; and one only says "رَفْثَ بامرَأَتِه", and one does not say "إلى امرأته". In my view this is like what is permissible of the "باء" in place of "إلى" in [His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَقَدْ أَحْسَنَ بَيۤ إِذْ أَخْرَجَنِي مِنَ ٱلسِّجْنِ﴾, which is only "أحسن اليّ" ("He was good to me"), so He did not [use] "إلى" and put the "باء" in its place], and in place of "على" in His saying ﴿فَأَثَابَكُمْ غَمَّاً بِغَمٍّ﴾, which is only "distress upon distress", [and His saying] ﴿وَمِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ مَنْ إِن تَأْمَنْهُ بِقِنْطَارٍ﴾, i.e. "with [lit. upon] a heap of gold", just as you say "مررتُ بِهِ" and "مررت عَلَيْهِ" ("I passed by him"), and as the poet said — and one whom I trust told me that he heard it from the Arabs — [in the wāfir metre; it is the twenty-fourth shāhid]:
[Translator's note: "twenty-fourth" is as written; it does not fit the surrounding sequence.]
إذا رَضِيَتْ عَلَيَّ بَنُو قُشَيْرٍ * لَعَمْرُ اللّهِ أَعْجَبَنِي رِضاها
(When the Banū Qushayr are pleased with me — by the life of Allah — their pleasure delights me.)
He means "عنى" [Translator's note: printed thus; i.e. «عنّي», "with me"]. And this resembles ﴿وَإِذَا خَلَوْاْ إِلَىٰ شَيَاطِينِهِمْ﴾, because you say "خَلَوْتُ إلَيْهِ وصنعنا كذا وكذا" ("I was alone with him and we did such-and-such") and "خَلَوْتُ به". And if you wish, you may take it in the meaning of His saying ﴿مَنْ أَنصَارِيۤ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ﴾, i.e. "with Allah", and as He said ﴿وَنَصَرْنَاهُ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ﴾, i.e. "against the people".

akhfash:84-84.t:
[And His saying] ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَاقَكُمْ لاَ تَسْفِكُونَ دِمَآءَكُمْ﴾: this is nominative because every verb of the forms "يَفْعَلُ هو", "تَفْعَل أنت", "أَفْعلٌ أَنا" and "نَفْعَلُ نَحن" [i.e. the imperfect] is always nominative (marfūʿ), and nothing governs it except the particles I mentioned to you: the particles of the accusative, or the particles of the jussive, command, prohibition and condition. None of these is here; it is only nominative because of its occurring in the position of nouns. The meaning of this speech is reported speech (ḥikāya), as though He said "We made them swear: they will not worship", i.e. We said to them: "By Allah, you will not worship"; that is because it is read ﴿يَعْبُدون﴾ and ﴿تَعْبُدون﴾. He said ﴿وَحِفْظاً مِّن كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ مَّارِدٍ﴾ ﴿لاَّ يَسَّمَّعُونَ إِلَىٰ ٱلْمَلإِ ٱلأَعْلَىٰ وَيُقْذَفُونَ﴾: if you wish, you may make "لا يَسَّمَّعُون" a new beginning (mubtadaʾ clause); and if you wish, you may say: it has the meaning of "أنْ لا لا يَسَّمَّعُوا" [Translator's note: «لا» is printed twice] — so when "أنْ" was dropped, it became nominative, just as you say "أَتَيْتُكَ تُعْطِيني وتُحْسِنُ إِلَيَّ وتَنْظُرُ في حاجتي" ("I came to you [so that] you give me, treat me well and see to my need"). Like it is "مُرْهُ يُعطِيني" ("order him [to] give me"): if you wish, you take it as "and he will give me", and if you wish, as "that he give me"; so when you dropped "أَنْ", it became nominative. The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the hundred and seventh shāhid (evidentiary verse)]:
أ‌لا أَيُّهذا الزاجِرِي احضر الوغي‌ * وأَنْ أَتْبَعَ اللَّذَّاتِ هَلْ انت مُخْلِدِي
(O you who chide me for being present at battle and for pursuing pleasures — can you make me immortal?)
So "أَحْضُرَ" has the meaning of "أَنْ أُحْضُرَ" ("that I be present").

akhfash:85-85.t:
He said ﴿تَظَاهَرُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِٱلإِثْمِ وَالْعُدْوَانِ﴾: he took it from "تَتَظاهَرُونَ" and assimilated the tāʾ into the ẓāʾ, and that is how we read. It has also been read ﴿تَظاهَرون﴾, light, by dropping the second tāʾ, because it is added without [contributing] a meaning. And He said ﴿وَإِن يَأتُوكُمْ أَسْرىٰ﴾, and it has been read ﴿أُسَارَى﴾. That is because "أَسير" (captive) is [of the pattern] "فَعِيل", and it resembles "مَرِيضاً" (sick), because there is an affliction in him as there is in the sick person, and this is a "فَعِيل" like it; and they said for the plural of "المريض", "مَرْضى". And they said ﴿أُسارَى﴾, making it like "سكارَى" (drunk) and "كُسالىَ" (lazy), because the plural of "فَعْلان" that denotes an affliction may share with the plural of "فَعِيل" and the plural of "فَعِل", as in "حَبِطٌ", "حَبْطى" and "حُباطَى", and "حَبِجٌ", "حَبْجى" and "حُباجى" [both: having a swollen belly]. And they said ﴿أَسارى﴾, as they said ﴿سَكَارَىٰ﴾.
Some of them said ﴿تَفْدُوهم﴾, from "تَفْدِى", and some of them ﴿تُفادُوهم﴾, from "فادَى", "يُفادِي", and that is how we read; and all of that is correct.
And He said ﴿فَمَا جَزَآءُ مَن يَفْعَلُ ذٰلِكَ مِنكُمْ إِلاَّ خِزْيٌ﴾, and He said ﴿مَا هَـٰذَا إِلاَّ بَشَرٌ مِّثْلُكُمْ﴾ and ﴿وَمَآ أَمْرُنَآ إِلاَّ وَاحِدَةٌ﴾, in the nominative, because every khabar (predicate) of "ما" in which the bāʾ is not good is nominative, since "ما" is not likened to the verb in that position; it is only likened to the verb in the position where the bāʾ is good, because then it has the meaning of "ليس" with nothing sharing it. That is the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic ﴿مَا هَـٰذَا بَشَراً﴾. And Tamīm put it in the nominative, because it is not of their dialect to liken "ما" to the verb.
And He said ﴿ثُمَّ أَنْتُمْ هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ﴾, and in another place ﴿هَا أَنْتُمْ هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ﴾, like some of what we have mentioned, and it is frequent in the speech of the Arabs; the [particle of] attention (tanbīh) is repeated for emphasis. And you say "ها أَنَا هذا" ("here I am, this one") and "ها أَنْتَ هذا", making "هذا" refer to the one addressed; and you say "هذا أنت". Something stronger than this has come. Allah the Mighty and Majestic said ﴿مَآ إِنَّ مَفَاتِحَهُ لَتَنُوءُ بِٱلْعُصْبَةِ أُوْلِي ٱلْقُوَّةِ﴾, while it is the band that is weighed down by the keys. He said [it is the hundred and seventeenth shāhid (evidentiary verse), in the majzūʾ al-wāfir metre]:
تَنُوءُ بِها فَتُثْقِلُها * عَجِيزَتُها......
(Her buttocks weigh her down, and burden her …)
He means "she is weighed down by her buttocks", i.e. she does not rise except with effort after effort. The poet said [in the basīṭ metre; it is the hundred and eighteenth shāhid]:
مِثْلُ القَنافِذِ هَدَّاجُونَ قَدْ بَلَغَت * نَجْرانَ أَوْ بَلَغَتْ سَوآتِهِم هَجَرُ
(Like hedgehogs, creeping about by night — [their foul deeds] have reached Najrān, or Hajar has reached their foul deeds [i.e. as worded, with the roles reversed].)
He means that the foul deeds reached Hajar; and "هَجَرُ" is nominative because the ode rhymes in the nominative. Like this is the saying of the poet [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the hundred and nineteenth shāhid]:
وَتَلْحَقُ خَيْلٌ لا هَوادَةَ بَينَها * وتَشْقى الرِّماحُ بالضَياطِرةُ الحُمْرِ
(And horsemen with no truce between them overtake [one another], and the spears are made wretched by the red, bulky men.)
While it is the bulky men who are made wretched by the spears. "الضياطرةُ" are the bulky ones; their singular is "ضَيْطار", like "بَيْطار" (farrier). And like the saying of the poet [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the hundred and twentieth shāhid]:
لَقَدْ خِفْتُ حَتَّى ما تزَيدُ مَخافَتِي * عَلى وعِلٍ بِذِي الفَقارَةِ عاقِلِ
(I have feared until my fear does not exceed [that of] a mountain goat taking refuge at Dhū al-Faqāra.)
He means: until the fear of a mountain goat does not exceed my fear.

akhfash:88-88.t:
He said ﴿فَقَلِيلاً مَّا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾, and its interpretation is "so little do they believe"; "ما" is redundant (zāʾida), as He said ﴿فَبِمَا رَحْمَةٍ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ لِنتَ لَهُمْ﴾, saying "so by mercy from Allah"; and He said ﴿إِنَّهُ لَحَقٌّ مِّثْلَ مَآ أَنَّكُمْ تَنطِقُونَ﴾, i.e. "it is surely true, just as you speak". The addition of "ما" in the Quran and in speech in this way is frequent. He said [in the munsariḥ metre; it is the hundred and twenty-first shāhid (evidentiary verse)]:
‌لَوْ بَأَبانَيْنِ جاءَ يَخْطِبُها * خُضِّبَ ما أَنْفُ خاطِبٍ بِدَمِ
(Had he come to ask for her hand at Abānān, the nose of a suitor would have been dyed with blood.)
I.e. the nose of a suitor would have been dyed with blood.

akhfash:89-89.t:
He said ﴿وَلَمَّا جَآءَهُمْ كِتَابٌ مِّنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ مُصَدِّقٌ لِّمَا مَعَهُمْ وَكَانُواْ مِن قَبْلُ يَسْتَفْتِحُونَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُمْ مَّا عَرَفُواْ كَفَرُواْ بِهِ﴾. If it is said, "Where then is the answer to ﴿وَلَمَّا جَآءَهُمْ كِتَابٌ مِّنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ مُصَدِّقٌ لِّمَا مَعَهُمْ﴾?", I say: "Its [kind of] answer is frequent in the Quran, [and] it was dispensed with in this place since its meaning was known." Likewise in all speech, when it grows long, things come in it that have no answers in that place, and the meaning suffices without it, as in the saying of Allah the Mighty and Majestic ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّ قُرْآناً سُيِّرَتْ بِهِ ٱلْجِبَالُ أَوْ قُطِّعَتْ بِهِ ٱلأَرْضُ أَوْ كُلِّمَ بِهِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ بَل للَّهِ ٱلأَمْرُ جَمِيعاً﴾: they mention [that] its interpretation is "if mountains were moved by a Quran other than this, this Quran would be one by which mountains are moved"; so the wording of the answer was dispensed with since the meaning was known. And He said ﴿لاَ تَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَفْرَحُونَ بِمَآ أَتَوْاْ وَّيُحِبُّونَ أَن يُحْمَدُواْ بِمَا لَمْ يَفْعَلُواْ فَلاَ تَحْسَبَنَّهُمْ بِمَفَازَةٍ مِّنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ﴾, and no answer [i.e. second object] came for the first "تحسَبَنَّ"; it was left out, being dispensed with by the answers in the Quran. And He said ﴿وَلاَ يَحْسَبَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَبْخَلُونَ بِمَآ آتَاهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ هُوَ خَيْراً لَّهُمْ﴾, whose meaning is "let them not think it good for them"; that speech was omitted, and in what remained there was an indication of the meaning. Like it is ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱتَّقُواْ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَمَا خَلْفَكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ﴾, then He said ﴿وَمَا تَأْتِيهِم مِّنْ آيَةٍ﴾ before bringing His saying "they did such-and-such", because that is frequent in the Quran, and it was dispensed with by it. And in His saying ﴿وَمَا تَأْتِيهِم مِّنْ آيَةٍ مِّنْ آيَاتِ رَبِّهِمْ إِلاَّ كَانُواْ عَنْهَا مُعْرِضِينَ﴾ there was an indication that they turned away, so this sufficed; and likewise everything in which the like of this is permissible. And He said ﴿فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعْدُ ٱلآخِرَةِ لِيَسُوءُواْ وُجُوهَكُمْ وَلِيَدْخُلُواْ ٱلْمَسْجِدَ كَمَا دَخَلُوهُ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ وَلِيُتَبِّرُواْ مَا عَلَوْاْ تَتْبِيراً﴾, and He said ﴿لِيُتَبَرِّواْ﴾ with the meaning "We left them and you alone; We did not protect you from them, because of your sins". And He said ﴿لِيَسُوءُواْ وُجُوهَكُمْ﴾ without mentioning that He left them and you alone, by way of abandonment in the state of trial for what they had previously done, and then did not prevent their enemies from being given power over them because of their wrongdoing. And He said ﴿وَلَوْ تَرَىۤ إِذِ ٱلظَّالِمُونَ فِي غَمَرَاتِ ٱلْمَوْتِ﴾, and there is no answer to this. And He said ﴿وَلَوْ يَرَى ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوۤاْ إِذْ يَرَوْنَ ٱلْعَذَابَ﴾, and the answer to this is only in the meaning; and this is frequent. We will explain everything we come across, if Allah wills. And they have claimed that this verse has no answer [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the hundred and twenty-second shāhid (evidentiary verse)]:
وَدَوِّيَّةٍ قَفْرٍ تَمَشّى نَعامُها * كَمَشْيِ النَّصارى في خِفافِ الأَرَنْدَجِ
(And many a barren desert, whose ostriches walk like Christians walking in boots of black leather.)
He means "and many a desert", and then he did not bring an answer for it. And he said [in the basīṭ metre; it is the hundred and twenty-third shāhid]:
حتَى إذا أسْلَكُوهُ في قُتائِدَةٍ * شَلاًّ كَما تَطْرُدُ الجَمالَةُ الشرُدُا
(Until, when they had driven them into [the pass of] Qutāʾida, driving hard, as camel-drivers drive the strays …)
This has no answer except in the meaning. And some of them claimed regarding this verse [in the kāmil metre; it is the hundred and fifth shāhid]:
فإذا وذلِكَ يا كُبَيْشَةُ لَمْ يكنْ * إلاّ كَلَمَّةِ حالِمٍ بِخِيالِ
(And then that, O Kubaysha, was nothing but like a dreamer's brief visit from a phantom.)
They said: the wāw in it is not redundant; rather, the khabar (predicate) is implied.

akhfash:90-90.t: He said ﴿بِئْسَمَا ٱشْتَرَوْاْ بِهِ أَنْفُسَهُمْ أَن يَكْفُرُواْ بِمَآ أنَزَلَ ٱللَّهُ بَغْياً أَن يُنَزِّلُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضْلِهِ﴾: ﴿ما﴾ by itself is a noun, and ﴿أَن يَكْفُرُواْ﴾ is an explanation of it, as in "نِعْمَ رَجُلاً زَيْدٌ" ("what an excellent man Zayd is"); and ﴿أَنْ يُنَزِّل﴾ is a badal (substitute) for ﴿بِمَآ أنَزَلَ ٱللَّهُ﴾.

akhfash:91-91.t:
He said ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلْحَقُّ مُصَدِّقاً لِّمَا مَعَهُمْ قُلْ فَلِمَ تَقْتُلُونَ أَنْبِيَآءَ ٱللَّهِ﴾: He put ﴿مُصَدِّقاً﴾ in the accusative because it is a khabar (predicate) [following] a definite [noun] [i.e. a ḥāl (circumstantial)]. And ﴿تَقْتُلُونَ﴾ has the meaning of "you killed", as the poet said [in the kāmil metre; it is the hundred and twenty-fourth shāhid (evidentiary verse)]:
وَلَقَدْ أمرُّ على اللَّئِيمِ يَسُبُّني * فَمَضَيْتُ ثُمَّتَ قُلتُ لا يَعْنِيني
(I pass by the base man who insults me, and I went on, then said: "He does not concern me".)
By his saying "أَمُرُّ" ("I pass") he means "I passed".

akhfash:96-96.t: His saying ﴿وَمَا هُوَ بِمُزَحْزِحِهِ مِنَ ٱلْعَذَابِ أَن يُعَمَّرَ﴾ is like "ما زَيْدٌ بِمُزَحْزِحِهِ أنْ يُعَمَّرَ" ("Zayd — his being given long life will not remove him") and "ما زَيْدٌ بِضارِّهِ أَنْ يقُومَ" ("Zayd — his standing will not harm him"). [So "أنْ يُعَمَّرَ"] is in the position of the nominative, and the bāʾ is good [here], just as you say "ما عبدُ الله بملازِمِهِ زَيْدٌ" ("ʿAbd Allāh — Zayd is not keeping close to him").

akhfash:97-97.t:
His saying ﴿مَن كَانَ عَدُوّاً لِّجِبْرِيلَ﴾: among the Arabs are those who say ﴿لِجِبرئِيلَ﴾; they use the hamza and they do not use it. Likewise ﴿إسرائيل﴾: some of them use the hamza and some do not. And they say ﴿مِيكائِيل﴾, using the hamza and not using it, and they say ﴿مِيكال﴾, just as they said ﴿جِبْرِيل﴾. Some of them said ﴿جبرعَل﴾, and I do not know [its rationale], except that I have heard ﴿إِسرائِل﴾. And some of them said ﴿إسْرِييلِ﴾, inclining (imāla) the rāʾ. Abū al-Ḥasan said: "In 'Jibrīl' there are six dialectal forms: جَبْراييل, جَبْرَئيل, جَبْرئِلْ
جَبْراعيل جَبْرَعِيل جَبرعل
and جَبْريل and جِبريلَ
فَعليل فِعليل
and جَبْرائِل.
جبراعل.
[Translator's note: the list is laid out as in the source, with what appear to be pattern equivalents (using ع as a stand-in for the hamza, and the measures فَعليل / فِعليل) on separate lines; more than six forms appear.]

akhfash:98-98.t:
He said ﴿مَن كَانَ عَدُوّاً للَّهِ وَمَلاۤئِكَتِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَجِبْرِيلَ وَمِيكَالَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَدُوٌّ لِّلْكَافِرِينَ﴾: He made the noun overt [instead of a pronoun] although He had mentioned it at the beginning of the speech. The poet said [in the kāmil metre; it is the hundred and twenty-fifth shāhid (evidentiary verse)]:
ليتَ الغُرابَ غَداةَ يَنْعَبُ دَائِباً * كانَ الغُرابُ مُقَطَّعَ الأوْداجِ
(Would that the crow, on the morning it croaks incessantly — that the crow had its jugular veins cut.)

akhfash:100-100.t: He said ﴿أَوَكُلَّمَا عَاهَدُواْ عَهْداً﴾: this is a wāw placed together with the interrogative particle, and it is like the fāʾ in His saying ﴿أَفَكُلَّمَا جَآءَكُمْ رَسُولٌ بِمَا لاَ تَهْوَىٰ أَنْفُسُكُمْ﴾. This is frequent in the Quran and in speech, and both are redundant (zāʾida) on this view. It is like the fāʾ in your saying "أَفَا الله لَتَصْنَعَنَّ كَذَا وكَذا" ("by Allah, you will surely do such-and-such!") and your saying to a man "أَفَلا تَقُوم" ("will you not stand?"). And if you wish, you may make the fāʾ and the wāw here a conjunction.

akhfash:102-102.t:
His saying ﴿وَمَآ أُنْزِلَ عَلَى ٱلْمَلَكَيْنِ بِبَابِلَ هَارُوتَ وَمَارُوتَ﴾: they [هاروت and ماروت] are maʿṭūf (conjoined) to ﴿ٱلْمَلَكَيْنِ﴾, or a badal (substitute) for them; but they are foreign, so they are diptotes, and their position is genitive. And ﴿بابلَ﴾ is a diptote because of its femininity. That is because the name of every feminine [entity] of two letters, or of three letters with the middle one quiescent, is fully declinable; and whatever feminine [name] is other than that is a diptote as long as it is the name of a feminine [entity].
And He said ﴿حَتَّىٰ يَقُولاَ إِنَّمَا نَحْنُ فِتْنَةٌ فَلاَ تَكْفُرْ فَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مِنْهُمَا﴾: His saying ﴿فَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ﴾ is not an answer to His saying ﴿فَلاَ تَكْفُرْ﴾; it is only a new beginning (mubtadaʾ), then He conjoined [something] to it and said ﴿وَيَتَعَلَّمُونَ مَا يَضُرُّهُمْ وَلاَ يَنفَعُهُمْ﴾. And He said ﴿يُفَرِّقُونَ بِهِ بَيْنَ ٱلْمَرْءِ وَزَوْجِهِ﴾, because each of them is a "زوج" (spouse): the woman is a زوج and the man is a زوج. He said ﴿وَخَلَقَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا﴾, and He said ﴿مِن كُلٍّ زَوْجَيْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ﴾. And "هُما زَوْجٌ" ("they are a pair") is also said of two, just as you say "هُما سَواءٌ" and "هُما سِيّانِ" ("they are alike"). [And "الزَوْج" is also the patterned cloth thrown over the camel-litter.] The poet said [in the kāmil metre; it is the hundred and twenty-sixth shāhid (evidentiary verse)]:
مِنْ كُلِّ مَحْفُوفٍ يظُلُّ غِصيَّةُ * زَوْجٌ عَلَيهِ كِلَّةٌ وَقِرامُها
([Women] in every covered litter, whose frame is shaded by a patterned cloth, with a canopy over it and its curtain.)
And they have said "الزَوْجَة" (wife). The poet said [in the basīṭ metre; it is the hundred and twenty-seventh shāhid]:
زَوْجَةُ أَشْمَطَ مَرْهُوبٍ بَوادِرُهُ * قَدْ صارَ في رَأْسِهِ التَخْويصُ والنزَعُ
(The wife of a grizzled man whose outbursts are feared, on whose head greying and receding hair have appeared.)
And He said ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمُواْ لَمَنِ ٱشْتَرَاهُ مَا لَهُ فِي ٱلآخِرَةِ مِنْ خَلاَقٍ﴾: this is the lām of ibtidāʾ (the inceptive lām), which enters after [verbs of] knowing and the like, and a new clause begins after it. You say "لَقَدْ علمت لَزَيدٌ خيرٌ منك" ("I knew that Zayd is indeed better than you"). He said ﴿لَّمَن تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ لأَمْلأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ﴾, and He said ﴿لَيُوسُفُ وَأَخُوهُ أَحَبُّ إِلَىٰ أَبِينَا مِنَّا﴾.
And He said ﴿وَلَقَدْ عَلِمُواْ لَمَنِ ٱشْتَرَاهُ﴾, then He said ﴿لَوْ كَانُواْ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾: by the first He means the devils, because they had known; and [by] ﴿ولَّوْ كَانُواْ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ He means humans. And in His saying ﴿لَمَثُوبَةٌ﴾ there was an indication of "they would have been rewarded", so the answer was dispensed with by it.

akhfash:103-103.t: He said ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ آمَنُواْ وٱتَّقَوْا لَمَثُوبَةٌ مِّنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ خَيْرٌ﴾: His saying ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ آمَنُواْ وٱتَّقَوْا﴾ has no answer in the wording, but [it has one] in the meaning: He means "they would have been rewarded". His saying ﴿لَمَثَوبَةٌ﴾ indicates "they would have been rewarded", so the answer was dispensed with by it. And in His saying ﴿لَمَثُوبَةٌ﴾ this lām is the lām of ibtidāʾ (the inceptive lām), as I explained to you.

akhfash:105-105.t: He said ﴿مَّا يَوَدُّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ وَلاَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾, i.e. "nor of the idolaters" — they do not wish ﴿أَن يُنَزَّلَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾.

akhfash:106-106.t: He said ﴿مَا نَنسَخْ مِنْ آيَةٍ أَوْ نُنسِهَا نَأْتِ بِخَيْرٍ مِّنْهَا أَوْ مِثْلِهَا﴾, and some of them said ﴿نَنْسَأْها﴾, i.e. "We postpone it". It is like ﴿إِنَّمَا ٱلنَّسِيۤءُ زِيَادَةٌ فِي ٱلْكُفْرِ﴾, because it is postponement. [And] "النَسِيئَةُ" (deferment of payment) and "النَسِيءُ" have one origin, from "أنسأت", except that you say "أَنْسَأتُ الشَيْءَ", i.e. I postponed the thing, and its maṣdar (verbal noun) is "النَسِيءُ"; and "أَنْسَأْتُكَ الدَيْنَ", i.e. I let you postpone the debt. It is as though he said "أَنْسَأْتُكَ" so "نَسَأْتُ". And "النَسِيء" is that they used to insert a month into a month. And some of them said ﴿أَوْ نَنْسَها﴾; all of that is correct. It is jussive by the condition. And al-nasīʾ with respect to the month is postponement.

akhfash:108-108.t: He said ﴿أَمْ تُرِيدُونَ أَن تَسْأَلُواْ رَسُولَكُمْ كَمَا سُئِلَ مُوسَىٰ مِن قَبْلُ﴾; and whoever lightens [the hamza] says ﴿سُيِل﴾. If it is said: "How did you make it 'between-between' (bayna bayna), when it would be between a quiescent yāʾ and the hamza, and a quiescent yāʾ does not come after a ḍamma, while the sīn has a ḍamma?", I say: "As for [the pattern] 'فُعِلَ', a quiescent yāʾ may come after a ḍamma, because they have said 'قُيْل' and 'بُيْعَ'. And the yāʾ in some [forms of] 'فُعِلَ' may become a pure wāw because of the ḍamma before it, being with it in one word, just as you say 'لم تَوْطُؤ الدابَّةُ' and as you say 'قَدْ رُؤِس فلان' ('so-and-so has been made chief')."

akhfash:111-111.t: He said ﴿لَن يَدْخُلَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ إِلاَّ مَن كَانَ هُوداً أَوْ نَصَارَىٰ﴾: they claimed that "الهُود" is the plural of "الهائِد", and "الهائد" is the penitent who returns to the truth. And He said in another place ﴿وَقَالُواْ كُونُواْ هُوداً﴾, i.e. be returners to the truth. [And one says] "هائِد" and "هُوَّد", like "ناقِه" [and "نُقَّه" (convalescent), and] "عائِدْ" and "عُوَّد", "حائِل" and "حُوَّل", and "بازِل" and "بُزَّل". He made ﴿مَن كَانَ﴾ singular because the wording of ﴿مَنْ﴾ is singular, and He used the plural in His saying ﴿هُوداً أَوْ نَصَارَىٰ﴾. On this aspect you say "مَنْ كانَ صاحبك" ("whoever were your companion[s]").

akhfash:114-114.t:
He said ﴿وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنْ مَّنَعَ مَسَاجِدَ ٱللَّهِ أَن يُذْكَرَ فِيهَا ٱسْمُهُ﴾: it is only "from His name being mentioned in them", but prepositions are frequently dropped with "أَنْ", and what precedes governs it, so that it is in the position of the accusative [i.e. accusative by removal of the preposition]. Or ﴿أَن يُذْكَرَ﴾ is a badal (substitute) for "المَساجِد"; they mean: "who is more unjust than one who prevented [His name] being mentioned".
And He said ﴿وَسَعَىٰ فِي خَرَابِهَآ﴾: this is on [the pattern of] "مَنَعَ" and "سَعَى" [i.e. singular verbs, following the wording of «مَنْ»]; then He said ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ مَا كَانَ لَهُمْ أَن يَدْخُلُوهَآ إِلاَّ خَآئِفِينَ﴾, making it plural, because ﴿مَنْ﴾ may have the meaning of a group.

akhfash:115-115.t: He said ﴿فَأَيْنَمَا تُوَلُّواْ فَثَمَّ وَجْهُ ٱللَّهِ﴾, because ﴿أَيْنَما﴾ is one of the jussive particles of the condition, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is in the fāʾ.

akhfash:117-117.t:
He said ﴿وَإِذَا قَضَىٰ أَمْراً فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ﴾: He put it in the nominative by conjunction, as though He only meant to say "He only says 'Be', and it is". Its nominative may also be on the basis of ibtidāʾ (a new beginning). And He said ﴿إِذَآ أَرَدْنَاهُ أَن نَّقُولَ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ﴾: if you make ﴿يَكُون﴾ here conjoined, you put it in the accusative, because ﴿أَنْ نَقُولَ﴾ is accusative by "أَنْ", as though He meant ﴿أَنْ نَقُولَ﴾ ﴿فيكونَ﴾. If he says: "How so, when the fāʾ is not in this meaning?", [the answer is that] the fāʾ and the wāw may conjoin to what precedes them and what follows them even if it is not in its meaning, as in "ما أنتَ وزيداً" ("what have you to do with Zayd?"), while he only means "you did not strike Zayd" [Translator's note: translated as written]; and you put it in the nominative on [the basis of] "what are you, and what is Zayd?", though that is not its meaning. And like your saying "إيّاكَ والأَسَدَ" ("beware of the lion"). The nominative in His saying ﴿فيَكُونُ﴾ is on the basis of ibtidāʾ, as in His saying ﴿لِّنُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ وَنُقِرُّ فِي ٱلأَرْحَامِ مَا نَشَآءُ﴾; and He said ﴿لِيُضِلَّ عَن سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ وَيَتَّخِذَهَا هُزُواً﴾. The accusative is also possible in His saying ﴿ويَتَّخَذَها﴾ and in ﴿نُقِرَّ في الأرْحامِ﴾, [conjoined] to the beginning of the speech. The poet said, using the nominative on the basis of ibtidāʾ [in the wāfir metre; it is the hundred and twenty-eighth shāhid (evidentiary verse)]:
‌‌يُعالِجُ عاقِراً أَعْيَتْ عَلَيْهِ * لِيَلْقِحَها فَيَنْتِجُها حُوارا
(He works on a barren [she-camel] who has defeated him, to impregnate her, and then she bears him a young camel.)
And the poet also said [in the ṭawīl metre; it is the hundred and twenty-ninth shāhid]:
وما هُوَ إلاّ أَنَّ أَراها فُجاءَةً * فَأَبْهَتُ حَتَّى ما أَكَادُ أُجِيبُ
(It is nothing but that I see her suddenly, and I am struck dumb, so that I can hardly reply.)
The accusative in his saying ﴿فأَبْهَتُ﴾ is by conjunction, and the nominative is on the basis of ibtidāʾ.

daas-irab:1-5.t:
﴿الم﴾: disjointed letters (ḥurūf muqaṭṭaʿa) with no grammatical position, or a khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هذه ألم" (this is Alif Lām Mīm). ﴿ذلِكَ﴾: ذا is a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address. ﴿الْكِتابُ﴾: a badal (substitute) from the demonstrative, nominative; it may also be parsed as the khabar of the demonstrative. ﴿لا رَيْبَ﴾: لا is the lā of generic negation, working like إنّ. ريب is its noun, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of accusative. ﴿فِيهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar, its implied form being "حاصل" (existing); the clause لا ريب فيه is a khabar of the demonstrative. ﴿هُدىً﴾: a second khabar of the demonstrative, nominative with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma.
﴿لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾: المتقين is a noun, genitive with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; both are attached to هدى. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of المتقين. ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is an attached pronoun in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent). ﴿بِالْغَيْبِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to the verb يؤمنون. The clause ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَيُقِيمُونَ﴾: its i'rab is like يؤمنون ... and the clause is conjoined to the clause before it. ﴿الصَّلاةَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَمِمَّا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and من is a preposition; ما is a relative noun, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of genitive by the preposition. ﴿رَزَقْناهُمْ﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn; نا is the fāʿil, the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi, and the mīm is the sign of the masculine plural. The returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, and it is the second object; the implied form is "مما رزقناهم إياه" (of what We provided them with it), and the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿يُنْفِقُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾: maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the relative noun before it. ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿بِما﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition; ما is a relative noun in the position of genitive by the preposition. ﴿أُنْزِلَ﴾: a passive past verb; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو" (it), referring back to ما.
﴿إِلَيْكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to the verb أنزل; the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿وَما أُنْزِلَ﴾: its i'rab is like the i'rab of the preceding one, and the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِكَ﴾: both attached to the verb أنزل; the kāf is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).
﴿وَبِالْآخِرَةِ﴾: both attached to the verb يوقنون. ﴿هُمْ﴾: a detached nominative pronoun, indeclinable on sukūn, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is conjoined to the clause يؤمنون. ﴿يُوقِنُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ هم.
﴿أُولئِكَ﴾: a demonstrative, indeclinable on kasra, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the kāf is for address. ﴿عَلى هُدىً﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to an omitted khabar; the implied form is "أولئك سائرون على هدى" (those are proceeding upon guidance). ﴿مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ﴾: both attached to an omitted naʿt of هدى, the implied form being "هدى نازل" (guidance sent down); the clause أولئك is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَأُولئِكَ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; أولئك is a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ. ﴿هُمُ﴾: a second mubtadaʾ, a detached pronoun. ﴿الْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾: khabar of هم, nominative with the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause هم المفلحون is the khabar of أولئك.

daas-irab:165-165.t:
﴿وَمِنَ﴾ The wāw is resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya). ﴿مِنَ النَّاسِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿مِنَ﴾ a relative noun in the position of the nominative (in the position of rafʿ) as a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). [Translator's note: the source prints the word as ﴿مِنَ﴾; the relative noun meant here is ﴿مَنْ﴾.] ﴿يَتَّخِذُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) being implied as "huwa" (he), referring back to مَن; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.
﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to يتخذ. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿أَنْداداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يُحِبُّونَهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb; the wāw is the fāʿil and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi; the clause is a ṣifa (adjective) of أندادا. ﴿كَحُبِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to an omitted ṣifa of a maṣdar (verbal noun) functioning as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "a great love". ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive or circumstantial (ḥāliyya); الذين is a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿أَشَدُّ﴾ khabar of the relative noun. ﴿حُبًّا﴾ tamyīz (specification). ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty is genitive (majrūr), and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the maṣdar حبا; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلَوْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive; لو is a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿يَرَى﴾ an imperfect verb.
﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, fāʿil (agent). ﴿ظَلَمُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the clause يرى الذين is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) for past time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يرى; it has also been said that it is in the sense of إذا, and so would be an adverb for future time. ﴿يَرَوْنَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. ﴿الْعَذابَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿أَنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿الْقُوَّةَ﴾ its noun (ism). ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty; they are a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate). ﴿جَمِيعاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); أنّ with its noun and khabar are interpreted as a maṣdar (interpreted maṣdar) standing in place of the two objects of يرى, and the apodosis (jawāb) of لو is omitted, its implied form being "they would have found an astonishing matter". ﴿وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ﴾ أنّ, the Name of Majesty is its noun and شديد is its khabar; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūfa). ﴿الْعَذابَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). [Translator's note: the muḍāf ilayhi here is written ﴿الْعَذابَ﴾ with fatḥa in the source; in the Quranic text it is ﴿الْعَذابِ﴾.]

daas-irab:166-167.t:
﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb for past time; it is a badal (substitute) from إذ in the preceding verse. ﴿تَبَرَّأَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿اتُّبِعُوا﴾ a passive past verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿مِنَ الَّذِينَ﴾ both attached to تبرأ. ﴿اتُّبِعُوا﴾ a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. [Translator's note: the source prints this second word as ﴿اتُّبِعُوا﴾, but its analysis (active verb with fāʿil) corresponds to the Quranic ﴿اتَّبَعُوا﴾.] ﴿وَرَأَوُا﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); رأوا is a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, with قد implied before it. ﴿الْعَذابَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَتَقَطَّعَتْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; تقطع is a past verb and the tāʾ is for the feminine. ﴿بِهِمُ﴾ both attached to تقطعت. ﴿الْأَسْبابُ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَقالَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿اتَّبَعُوا﴾ a past verb and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿لَوْ﴾ a conditional particle containing the sense of wishing (tamannī). ﴿أَنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿لَنا﴾ both attached to an omitted khabar of أنّ. ﴿كَرَّةً﴾ its noun; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying). ﴿فَنَتَبَرَّأَ﴾ the fāʾ is causal (al-sababiyya); نتبرأ is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an أن concealed after the fāʾ, and its fāʿil is implied as "naḥnu" (we). ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ both attached to نتبرأ; أن and the verb are interpreted as a maṣdar conjoined to a maṣdar implied from the preceding verb, the implied form being: "we want a return and a disavowal of these". ﴿كَما﴾ the kāf is a preposition; ما is maṣdariyya (infinitival).
﴿تَبَرَّؤُا﴾ a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the maṣdariyya ما with the verb is interpreted as a maṣdar in the position of the genitive by the kāf, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ṣifa (adjective) of an omitted accusative maṣdar functioning as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), its implied form being: "we disavow like their disavowal".
﴿مِنَّا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to the verb before them. ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to an omitted ṣifa of an omitted maṣdar, a mafʿūl muṭlaq, its implied form being: "Allah shows them a showing like that showing". ﴿يُرِيهِمُ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ because of heaviness, and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil. ﴿أَعْمالَهُمْ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿حَسَراتٍ﴾ ḥāl.
﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to حسرات; the clause كذلك is resumptive. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; ما is the Ḥijāzī mā, which operates like ليس. ﴿هُمْ﴾ a detached pronoun, the noun of ما. ﴿بِخارِجِينَ﴾ the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); خارجين is a noun genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar of ما. ﴿مِنَ النَّارِ﴾ both attached to خارجين.

daas-irab:234-234.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾: the wāw is resumptive; الذين is a relative noun, in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يُتَوَفَّوْنَ﴾: a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَيَذَرُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined. ﴿أَزْواجاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يَتَرَبَّصْنَ﴾: an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, and the nūn of the feminine plural is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "the wives of those who die among you wait"; and this nominal clause is the khabar of الذين. ﴿بِأَنْفُسِهِنَّ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb before them. ﴿أَرْبَعَةَ﴾: an adverb of time, attached to the verb before it. ﴿أَشْهُرٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (the genitive term of the construct). ﴿وَعَشْراً﴾: conjoined to أربعة, i.e. ten nights.

daas-irab:235-235.t:
﴿فَإِذا﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive; إذا is an adverb of time. ﴿بَلَغْنَ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿أَجَلَهُنَّ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: its i'rab has been given before; the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. ﴿فِيما﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَعَلْنَ﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, and the nūn of the feminine plural is the fāʿil. ﴿فِي أَنْفُسِهِنَّ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to فعلن.
﴿بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "acting according to what is recognized (bi-l-maʿrūf)". ﴿وَاللَّهُ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرٌ﴾: the i'rab of its like has preceded in the previous verse.
﴿وَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيما عَرَّضْتُمْ بِهِ﴾: for its i'rab see verse 228. ﴿مِنْ خِطْبَةِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿النِّساءِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (the genitive term of the construct). ﴿أَوْ أَكْنَنْتُمْ﴾: أو is a conjunction; أكننتم is a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أكننتم; the clause is conjoined. ﴿عَلِمَ اللَّهُ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿أَنَّكُمْ﴾: anna and its noun. ﴿سَتَذْكُرُونَهُنَّ﴾: the sīn is for the future; تذكروهن is an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as the khabar (predicate) of anna; and anna with what follows it stands in place of the two objects of عَلِمَ. The clause ﴿عَلِمَ اللَّهُ ... ﴾ is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَلكِنْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لكن is a particle of rectification (istidrāk). ﴿لا﴾: prohibitive, making the verb jussive. ﴿تُواعِدُوهُنَّ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil and the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿سِرًّا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi; it is also said to be a ḥāl, or accusative by removal of the preposition. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: particle of exception. ﴿أَنْ تَقُولُوا﴾: the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from the maṣdar-particle an and the imperfect verb after it is in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as the excepted. ﴿قَوْلًا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿مَعْرُوفاً﴾: an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿وَلا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive, making the verb jussive. ﴿تَعْزِمُوا﴾: a jussive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿عُقْدَةَ﴾: accusative by removal of the preposition, its implied form being: "upon (ʿalā) the knot".
﴿النِّكاحِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ﴾: the interpreted maṣdar formed from the an latent after ḥattā and the verb يبلغ is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by the preposition, and the two are attached to تعزموا. ﴿الْكِتابُ﴾: fāʿil. ﴿أَجَلَهُ﴾: mafʿūl bihi.
﴿وَاعْلَمُوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; اعلموا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾: anna, and the Name of Majesty is its noun; and the clause ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ is its khabar; and anna with what follows it stands in place of the two objects of اعلموا. ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فِي أَنْفُسِكُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فَاحْذَرُوهُ﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa. ﴿احذروه﴾: an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَاعْلَمُوا﴾: an imperative verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ﴾: anna, the Name of Majesty is its noun, and غفور is its khabar. ﴿حَلِيمٌ﴾: a second khabar. And anna with what follows it stands in place of the two objects of اعلموا. The clause اعلموا is conjoined.

daas-irab:236-236.t:
﴿لا جُناحَ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: lā, its noun and its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنْ﴾: a conditional particle that makes the verb jussive. ﴿طَلَّقْتُمُ﴾: a past verb, and the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent); it is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿النِّساءَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive. ﴿ما لَمْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ﴾: ما is the temporal maṣdar-particle; لم makes the verb jussive; تمسوهن is an imperfect verb, jussive by the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; and the maṣdar-particle ما with the verb is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of genitive by ḥattā, and the two are attached to the verb before them. [Translator's note: so in the source — there is no حتى in the verse; the intended sense is presumably an implied temporal adverb ("as long as").] ﴿أَوْ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿تَفْرِضُوا﴾: conjoined to تمسوهن.
Some said that أو here means: "unless you assign (illā an tafriḍū)" ... and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted. ﴿لَهُنَّ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them. ﴿فَرِيضَةً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ﴾: the clause is conjoined to the omitted apodosis. ﴿عَلَى الْمُوسِعِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿قَدَرُهُ﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause or resumptive. ﴿وَعَلَى الْمُقْتِرِ قَدَرُهُ﴾: conjoined.
﴿مَتاعاً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to متاعا. ﴿حَقًّا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb. ﴿عَلَى الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to حقا.

daas-irab:237-237.t:
﴿وَإِنْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿إِنْ﴾: a conditional particle that makes the verb jussive. ﴿طَلَّقْتُمُوهُنَّ﴾: a past verb; the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent) and the hāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the mīm was given a ḍamma for lengthening (ishbāʿ); it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them. ﴿أَنْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ﴾: the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from the verb and the subjunctive-making an is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَقَدْ﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); قد is a particle of verification (taḥqīq). ﴿فَرَضْتُمْ﴾: a verb and its fāʿil. ﴿لَهُنَّ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to فرضتم. ﴿فَرِيضَةً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَنِصْفُ﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); نصف is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "then what is due is half", or it is a mubtadaʾ, the implied form being "then upon you is half"; the clause is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis.
﴿ما فَرَضْتُمْ﴾: ما is a relative noun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction or of exception. ﴿إِنْ﴾: a maṣdar-particle that makes the verb subjunctive. [Translator's note: so in the source, written ﴿إِنْ﴾; the verse reads أَنْ.] ﴿يَعْفُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, and the nūn of the feminine plural is the fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of genitive by a preposition, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), the implied form being: "then half of what you assigned, except in the case of their pardoning". ﴿أَوْ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿يَعْفُوَا﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) with fatḥa, conjoined. ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a relative noun, fāʿil. ﴿بِيَدِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar. ﴿عُقْدَةُ﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿النِّكاحِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾: the wāw is resumptive. [Translator's note: so in the source, written ﴿وَإِنْ﴾; the verse reads وَأَنْ.] ﴿أَنْ تَعْفُوا﴾: the interpreted maṣdar formed from the verb and the subjunctive-making an is in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: "and pardoning ...".
﴿أَقْرَبُ﴾: khabar. ﴿لِلتَّقْوى﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أقرب. ﴿وَلا تَنْسَوُا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لا is prohibitive, making the verb jussive; تنسوا is a jussive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿الْفَضْلَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿بَيْنَكُمْ﴾: an adverb of place, attached to an omitted ḥāl from الفضل; the clause is conjoined.
﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾: inna, and the Name of Majesty is its noun. ﴿بَصِيرٌ﴾: its khabar. ﴿بِما﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to بصير; and the clause ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ is the ṣila of the relative noun; and the clause ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:86-86.t: ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, khabar (predicate). ﴿اشْتَرَوُا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿الْحَياةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾ an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿بِالْآخِرَةِ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) اشتروا. ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; lā is negative. ﴿يُخَفَّفُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb. ﴿عَنْهُمُ﴾ attached to the verb before them. ﴿الْعَذابُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf). ﴿وَلا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ the nominal clause is conjoined, and the verbal clause is the khabar.

daas-irab:87-87.t:
﴿قَفَّيْنا﴾ قفّاه originally means "he followed his track". القفا is the back of the neck, and from it comes قافية الشعر (the rhyme of a poem).
﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath; qad is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq). ﴿آتَيْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿مُوسَى﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿الْكِتابَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. The clause is the response to the oath, a clause with no grammatical position. ﴿وَقَفَّيْنا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf). ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِهِ بِالرُّسُلِ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb قفينا; the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَآتَيْنا عِيسَى﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi. ﴿ابْنَ﴾ badal (substitute). ﴿مَرْيَمَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) with the fatḥa in place of the kasra, being a foreign proper name. ﴿الْبَيِّناتِ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) with the kasra, being a sound feminine plural. The clause آتينا is conjoined. ﴿وَأَيَّدْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿بِرُوحِ﴾ attached to أيدناه. ﴿الْقُدُسِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَفَكُلَّما﴾ the hamza is for interrogation, the fāʾ is resumptive; كلما is a mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial), an adverb of time containing the sense of a condition and attached to its apodosis. ﴿جاءَكُمْ﴾ a past verb and a fronted mafʿūl bihi. ﴿رَسُولٌ﴾ a postponed fāʿil; the clause is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بِما﴾ attached to an adjective of رسول. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿تَهْوى﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif due to impossibility (taʿadhdhur). ﴿أَنْفُسُكُمُ﴾ fāʿil, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. [Translator's note: the source says "the hāʾ", though the attached pronoun here is كم.] ﴿فَفَرِيقاً﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and فريقا is a mafʿūl bihi fronted before the past verb. ﴿كَذَّبْتُمْ﴾ and the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَفَرِيقاً تَقْتُلُونَ﴾ the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:88-89.t:
﴿وَقالُوا﴾ the wāw is resumptive; قالوا is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿قُلُوبُنا غُلْفٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of conjunction and digression (iḍrāb). ﴿لَعَنَهُمُ﴾ a past verb and mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, fāʿil. ﴿بِكُفْرِهِمْ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them. ﴿فَقَلِيلًا﴾ the fāʾ is resumptive; قليلا is an adjective of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), the implied form being "so they do not believe except with a little belief". ﴿ما﴾ a vague indefinite, an adjective of قليل. It is also said to be maṣdariyya, and the interpreted maṣdar is the fāʿil of قليل, the implied form being "little is their belief". The clause is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. ﴿وَلَمَّا﴾ the wāw is resumptive; lammā is adverbial (ẓarfiyya) in the sense of "when" (ḥīniyya), conditional. ﴿جاءَهُمْ كِتابٌ﴾ a past verb, mafʿūl bihi and fāʿil. ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِ﴾ attached to an omitted adjective of كتاب. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مُصَدِّقٌ﴾ an adjective of كتاب. ﴿لَمَّا﴾ a relative noun in the position of genitive by the preposition; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to مصدق. [Translator's note: the source parses لِما (lām + mā) under this heading.] ﴿مَعَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of place attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَكانُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; kāna and its noun. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ min is a preposition; qablu is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of genitive by the preposition; it is made indeclinable because it is cut off from the iḍāfa, the original being "before that". The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the postponed verb يستفتحون; and the clause ﴿يَسْتَفْتِحُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its fāʿil, the clause being in the position of accusative as the khabar of kāna. ﴿عَلَى الَّذِينَ﴾ attached to يستفتحون. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿فَلَمَّا جاءَهُمْ ما عَرَفُوا﴾ lammā is adverbial, conditional and non-jussive; جاءهم is a past verb and its object; mā is a relative noun in the position of nominative as fāʿil, and the clause عرفوا is its ṣila. The clause فلما جاءهم is conjoined, and the clause جاءهم is in the position of genitive by iḍāfa. As for the clause ﴿كَفَرُوا بِهِ﴾, it is the apodosis (jawāb) of the conditional lammā. ﴿فَلَعْنَةُ﴾ the fāʾ is causal.
لعنة is mubtadaʾ. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ﴾ attached to an omitted khabar. The nominal clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:90-90.t:
﴿بِئْسَمَا﴾ بئس is a past verb for creating blame (inshāʾ al-dhamm); its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun in it, indicated by mā; mā is a complete indefinite (nakira tāmma), indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of accusative as tamyīz (specification), i.e. "evil is the purchase, a purchase…". ﴿اشْتَرَوْا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِهِ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) اشتروا. ﴿أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause is in the position of accusative as an adjective. ﴿أَنْ﴾ a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle. ﴿يَكْفُرُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb) by dropping the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil. أن and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is the clause بئس.
﴿بِما﴾ the bāʾ is a preposition; mā is a relative noun in the position of genitive by the preposition; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb before them.
﴿أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb, and the Name of Majesty is the fāʿil. ﴿بَغْياً﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative. ﴿أَنْ﴾ a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle.
﴿يُنَزِّلَ﴾ an imperfect verb, subjunctive; the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is in the position of genitive by a preposition, the implied form being "out of envy that Allah sends down". ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, its fāʿil. ﴿مِنْ فَضْلِهِ﴾ attached to ينزل. ﴿عَلى مَنْ﴾ attached to ينزل. ﴿يَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb; the fāʿil is "he", and the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, being the object. ﴿مِنْ عِبادِهِ﴾ attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of this object, i.e. "upon whomever He wills of His servants". The clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿فَباؤُ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; باءوا is a past verb and the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿بِغَضَبٍ﴾ attached to the verb before them. ﴿عَلى غَضَبٍ﴾ attached to an omitted adjective of the first غضب. The clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf). ﴿وَلِلْكافِرِينَ﴾ the wāw is resumptive; الكافرين is a noun, genitive (majrūr) with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿عَذابٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿مُهِينٌ﴾ an adjective; the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:91-91.t:
﴿وَإِذا قِيلَ لَهُمْ آمِنُوا بِما أَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ﴾ the i'rab of the like of this has preceded in verse 11 and the previous verse. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. ﴿نُؤْمِنُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil being "we" (naḥnu). ﴿بِما﴾ mā is a relative noun in the position of genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb نؤمن. ﴿أَنْزَلَ﴾ a passive past verb, and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is "it". ﴿عَلَيْنا﴾ attached to أنزل; the clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). [Translator's note: so in the source.] ﴿وَيَكْفُرُونَ﴾ the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf). ﴿بِما﴾ mā is a relative noun in the position of genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to يكفرون. ﴿وَراءَهُ﴾ mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial), an adverb of place attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial; هو is mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الْحَقُّ﴾ its khabar (predicate); the clause is circumstantial. ﴿مُصَدِّقاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative. ﴿لِما﴾ mā is a relative noun; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to مصدقا. ﴿مَعَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of place attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative noun.
﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "you". ﴿فَلِمَ﴾ the fāʾ is the faṣīḥa, because it discloses an implied condition: "if you are truthful in your claim, then why do you kill". ﴿لم﴾ the lām is a preposition; mā is an interrogative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn in the position of genitive by the lām; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the imperfect verb. ﴿تَقْتُلُونَ﴾ The alif of mā was dropped to distinguish between it and the informative (khabariyya) mā.
The clause تقتلون is the apodosis of the condition, and the condition with its apodosis is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). The clause قل is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿أَنْبِياءَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مِنْ﴾ a preposition. ﴿قَبْلُ﴾ a noun indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb تقتلون. ﴿إِنْ﴾ conditional. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the tāʾ is its noun; the mīm is for the masculine plural. ﴿مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ khabar, accusative (manṣūb) with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. The apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes it. The clause إن كنتم is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:92-93.t:
﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive; the lām occurs in the response to an oath; qad is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq). ﴿جاءَكُمْ﴾ a past verb, and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مُوسى﴾ a postponed fāʿil (agent). ﴿بِالْبَيِّناتِ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before them; the clause is resumptive. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿اتَّخَذْتُمُ﴾ a past verb, and the tāʾ is the fāʿil. ﴿الْعِجْلَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِهِ﴾ attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial), the implied form being "then you took the calf, disbelieving, after him". ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ ظالِمُونَ﴾
the wāw is circumstantial, and mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the clause is in the position of accusative as ḥāl. ﴿وَإِذْ أَخَذْنا مِيثاقَكُمْ وَرَفَعْنا فَوْقَكُمُ الطُّورَ خُذُوا ما آتَيْناكُمْ بِقُوَّةٍ وَاسْمَعُوا﴾ see verse 63.
﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿سَمِعْنا﴾ a past verb indeclinable on the sukūn, and نا is the fāʿil; and likewise ﴿وَعَصَيْنا﴾; the two clauses are the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَأُشْرِبُوا﴾ a passive past verb indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ﴾ attached to أشربوا, or to a ḥāl of العجل. ﴿الْعِجْلَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿بِكُفْرِهِمْ﴾ attached to أشربوا or to a ḥāl of العجل. ﴿الْعِجْلَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿بِكُفْرِهِمْ﴾ attached to أشربوا. [Translator's note: the last two items repeat in the source.] The clause أشربوا is circumstantial. ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb, and the fāʿil is "you"; the clause is resumptive. ﴿بِئْسَما يَأْمُرُكُمْ بِهِ إِيمانُكُمْ﴾ بئس is a past verb for creating blame (inshāʾ al-dhamm), and mā is its fāʿil; the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) has been omitted, namely the love of the calf and its worship. يأمركم is an imperfect verb, the kāf is its object, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). [Translator's note: so in the source; the overt noun إيمانكم is the fāʿil of يأمر.] ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ its i'rab has preceded with verse 91, and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, its implied form being "then why did you worship the calf?".

daas-irab:94-94.t:
﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is "you"; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنْ﴾ a jussive conditional particle. ﴿كانَتْ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the tāʾ is for the feminine. ﴿لَكُمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) خالصة. ﴿الدَّارُ﴾ the noun of kāna.
﴿الْآخِرَةُ﴾ an adjective of الدار. ﴿عِنْدَ﴾ mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial), an adverb of place attached to خالصة. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿خالِصَةً﴾ the khabar (predicate) of kāna; it is also said to be a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿مِنْ دُونِ﴾ attached to the active participle خالصة. ﴿النَّاسِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. The conditional clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿فَتَمَنَّوُا﴾ the fāʾ links the apodosis of the condition; تمنوا is an imperative verb indeclinable (mabnī) on dropping the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿الْمَوْتَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ﴾ like His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ in the previous verse.

daas-irab:95-96.t:
﴿وَلَنْ﴾ the wāw is resumptive; lan is a particle of negation, the subjunctive and futurity. ﴿يَتَمَنَّوْهُ﴾ an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb) by dropping the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent) and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَبَداً﴾ mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial), an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb before it. ﴿بِما﴾ mā is a relative noun in the position of genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to the verb يتمنوه. ﴿قَدَّمَتْ﴾ a past verb. ﴿أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ due to heaviness; the hāʾ is an attached pronoun in the position of genitive by iḍāfa; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the wāw is resumptive; the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive, and it is also said to be circumstantial. ﴿بِالظَّالِمِينَ﴾ genitive (majrūr) with the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to عليم.
﴿وَلَتَجِدَنَّهُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; the lām occurs in the response to an oath; تجدن is an imperfect verb indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because of its connection with the heavy nūn of emphasis, and the nūn of emphasis has no grammatical position; the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "you"; the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi, and the mīm is for the masculine plural. ﴿أَحْرَصَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿النَّاسِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿عَلى حَياةٍ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أحرص; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ﴾ الذين is a relative noun indeclinable on the fatḥa in the position of genitive by the preposition; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted element, its implied form being "and more eager than those who associated partners".
﴿أَشْرَكُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿يَوَدُّ﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿أَحَدُهُمْ﴾ fāʿil, nominative with the ḍamma; the clause is resumptive or circumstantial. ﴿لَوْ﴾ a maṣdar-forming particle. ﴿يُعَمَّرُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, nominative with the ḍamma; its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent pronoun implied as "he". The maṣdar-forming particle with the verb is interpreted as a maṣdar in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, the implied form being "one of them wishes long life". ﴿أَلْفَ﴾ an adverb of time attached to يعمر. ﴿سَنَةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is circumstantial; mā is the Ḥijāzī negative mā that operates like laysa. ﴿هُوَ﴾ a detached nominative pronoun in the position of nominative as its noun.
﴿بِمُزَحْزِحِهِ﴾ the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; مزحزحه is a noun genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar of mā. ﴿مِنَ الْعَذابِ﴾ attached to مزحزح. ﴿أَنْ﴾ a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle. ﴿يُعَمَّرُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, subjunctive, and its nāʾib fāʿil is latent; أن and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar in the position of nominative as the fāʿil of the active participle مزحزح. The clause ما هو بمزحزحه is circumstantial. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ. ﴿بَصِيرٌ﴾ khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿بِما﴾ the bāʾ is a preposition; mā is a relative or maṣdar-forming particle in the position of genitive by the preposition; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to بصير.
﴿يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. The returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted: "of what they do (it)".

daas-irab:238-239.t: ﴿حافِظُوا﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). ﴿عَلَى الصَّلَواتِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) حافظوا. ﴿وَالصَّلاةِ﴾: conjoined to الصلوات. ﴿الْوُسْطى﴾: an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿وَقُومُوا﴾: conjoined to حافظوا. ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty, genitive (majrūr) by the lām; the two are attached to قانتين. ﴿قانِتِينَ﴾: a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb) with yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. The clause ﴿حافِظُوا﴾ is parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya), and ﴿وَقُومُوا﴾ is conjoined to it. ﴿فَإِنْ خِفْتُمْ﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive; إن is conditional; خفتم is a past verb, it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the tāʾ is its fāʿil. ﴿فَرِجالًا﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); رجالا is a ḥāl, the implied form being: "then pray on foot"; the clause is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis. ﴿أَوْ رُكْباناً﴾: conjoined to رجالا. ﴿فَإِذا﴾: إذا is an adverb for future time. ﴿أَمِنْتُمْ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis; اذكروا الله: an imperative verb and its fāʿil, and the Name of Majesty is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. ﴿كَما عَلَّمَكُمْ﴾: the kāf is a preposition; ما is the maṣdar-particle and, with the verb علمكم, is interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of genitive by the kāf; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted adjective of a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun, second mafʿūl bihi of علمكم. ﴿لَمْ تَكُونُوا﴾: a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive by the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its noun, and the clause ﴿تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ is its khabar (predicate); the clause تكونوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.

daas-irab:240-240.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنْكُمْ وَيَذَرُونَ أَزْواجاً﴾: its i'rab preceded with verse 233. [Translator's note: so in the source; the passage parsed earlier is verse 234.] ﴿وَصِيَّةً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, the implied form being: "they bequeath a bequest"; the implied clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) الذين. ﴿لِأَزْواجِهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective of وصية. ﴿مَتاعاً﴾: an accusative ḥāl (circumstantial); it is also said to be a badal (substitute) from وصية. ﴿إِلَى الْحَوْلِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an adjective of متاع. ﴿غَيْرَ إِخْراجٍ﴾: غير is an accusative ḥāl, and it is also said to be an adjective of متاع; إخراج is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَإِنْ﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive; إن is conditional. ﴿خَرَجْنَ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿فَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي ما فَعَلْنَ فِي أَنْفُسِهِنَّ مِنْ مَعْرُوفٍ﴾: its i'rab preceded with verse 233. ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾: the wāw is resumptive; الله, the Name of Majesty, is the mubtadaʾ, and عزيز and حكيم are two khabars.

daas-irab:241-241.t: ﴿وَلِلْمُطَلَّقاتِ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; للمطلقات is a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿مَتاعٌ﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to متاع. ﴿حَقًّا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being: "that is due as a due". ﴿عَلَى الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to حقا.

daas-irab:243-243.t: ﴿أَلَمْ﴾: the hamza is interrogative; لم is a particle that makes the verb jussive. ﴿تَرَ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil (agent) is "you" (anta). ﴿إِلَى الَّذِينَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb تر. ﴿خَرَجُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿مِنْ دِيارِهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to خرجوا; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); هم is a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿أُلُوفٌ﴾: khabar (predicate). ﴿حَذَرَ﴾: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿الْمَوْتِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَقالَ﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; قال is a past verb. ﴿لَهُمُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to قال. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾: the Name of Majesty, fāʿil. ﴿مُوتُوا﴾: an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿أَحْياهُمْ﴾: a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is "he", referring to Allah. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾: inna, and the Name of Majesty is its noun. ﴿لَذُو﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa). ﴿ذو﴾: khabar, nominative (marfūʿ) with wāw because it is one of the five nouns. ﴿فَضْلٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَلَى النَّاسِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to فضل. ﴿وَلكِنَّ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لكن is a particle resembling the verb that conveys rectification (istidrāk). ﴿أَكْثَرَ﴾: its noun, accusative (manṣūb) with fatḥa. ﴿النَّاسِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لا يَشْكُرُونَ﴾: لا is negating; يشكرون is an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of nominative as the khabar of lākinna.

daas-irab:244-245.t: ﴿وَقاتِلُوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; قاتلوا is an imperative verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). ﴿فِي سَبِيلِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) قاتلوا. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾: the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is conjoined to an implied clause, the implied form being: "i.e. be patient and fight". ﴿وَاعْلَمُوا﴾: conjoined to قاتلوا. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾: anna, the Name of Majesty is its noun, and سميع and عليم are two khabars (predicates) of anna; and anna with what follows it stands in place of the two objects of اعلموا. ﴿مَنْ﴾: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿ذَا﴾: a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of nominative (marfūʿ) as khabar. ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a relative noun, in the position of nominative as an adjective of ذا; it is also said to be a badal (substitute); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿يُقْرِضُ اللَّهَ﴾: an imperfect verb, the Name of Majesty is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿قَرْضاً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) or mafʿūl bihi. ﴿حَسَناً﴾: an adjective. ﴿فَيُضاعِفَهُ﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ of causation (al-sababiyya); يضاعفه is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an an latent after the fāʾ of causation; the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is "he", referring to Allah. ﴿لَهُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to يضاعفه. ﴿أَضْعافاً﴾: a ḥāl (circumstantial) or mafʿūl muṭlaq. ﴿كَثِيرَةً﴾: an adjective. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾: the wāw is resumptive;
